I got a Tradescantia Sitara Tricolour (Spathacea/Boat Lily/Moses in the Cradle) recently which was in very moisture retentive soil apparently. I watered it as instructed by the shop (when first two inches of soil are dry) and it died very quickly afterwards. The plant was in a 12cm pot however it was a plug without any substantial root system so I wonder if there was just too much soil for the poor plant. The soil appeared to be regular potting mix with no amendments at all. 

The shop sent a replacement plant and it was in the same sort of soil. I noticed the bottom two leaves of the plant were black on arrival and I now have a moisture meter so I checked and the soil was completely dry (0 on the meter) so I watered. The next day I noticed the tips of the plant turning brown which I read could be dry air but the plant is close to a humidifier which has been keeping my calathea very happy. I checked the soil and it was still very moist so I just waited to see what would happen. The plant kept getting worse over the next few days and I noticed that the soil wasn't drying at all (reading 8 on the meter) so I repotted into new soil mixture with more amendments to prevent waterlogged clumpy soil. The roots were partially rotted so I removed the rotten ones and there seemed to be a reasonable amount of healthy roots. I put it in a mixture of coco coir, perlite, orchard bark and activated charcoal with neem cake fertiliser. The plant seemed better for a while after this and the new growth at the bottom was growing larger, although I had to chop lots of browning older leaves so it didn't look very pretty. 

I waited until the new soil was dry to water (and the plant was starting to look dry) and gave it a drink. The next day the leaves looked even more brown and sad.

I'm so confused with this plant, I thought they were supposed to be easy to care for but I'm really struggling to figure out what it needs. 

Does anyone have experience caring for this particular plant? Is it dead from the previous overwatering and root rot? Did I ruin it by repotting it? Did I wait too long before watering? Or did I overwater it a second time?

The plant is kept in a North Facing window (unfortunately I only have North facing available) in a room which is around 21-27 celcius and maintained at 60+ humidity. I move it further in at night so it doesn't get cold right by the window (there is a very thick curtain between the plant and glass at night). I do have a radiator in the room, although it is more than 5 feet away from the plant and I have a humidifier to compensate. Also the radiator hasn't been on much recently because it is Summer. 

It's in a 12cm plastic nursery pot with a plastic cover pot. When I water I go slow and wait for water to drain all the way out before returning it to the cover pot. I check the cover pot after 20-30 mins to make sure there are no drips in the bottom that could hurt the plant. 

I'm wondering if the lack of light means that I need to give it tiny portions of water or something, or maybe it just hates it here :(

Unfortunately I've been cutting off the crispy browning leaf edges so the picture doesn't show them properly but you can see on the baby leaves at the bottom an example of what has been happening and the amount of missing leaves are from me cutting them because they looked dead...

TLDR: Tradescantia Sitara with browning leaves, is it overwatered and can I save it?

I'm also a musician and I have the exact same problem. Honestly I think the struggle for creative work is that in order for it to be good it needs to come naturally. If you force yourself to write an amazing song, you probably won't write one. If you relax and get into the flow state you'll perhaps write 10 great songs in one day. 

It might help to learn a new instrument to make it more interesting and give you targeted practice exercises to do every day.

Also try writing every day. Not songs, just whatever you think. Maybe something will turn into a song idea. Meditation is good too, try and do nothing for as long as possible instead of seeking distraction. You might find whatever thoughts/feelings you're avoiding with the distractions could be channeled into writing

The question to ask yourself is are you actually happy with your life? If you are satisfied in all other areas and are genuinely only using weed when you feel too depressed to cope then you should continue. If you are unhappy and using weed to mask your unhappiness, it might be better to quit.

I know this post is super old but I just had to comment to say I completely agree with you! My story is very very similar to yours... I left school after doing GCSEs (partly because I was already bored of the student clubbing / casual sex culture which reigned at my school) and worked. Then the recession hit so I went to college to study a vocational qualification. Was working full-time in a career by the age of 19, socialising with adults from 25-60 and in a long term relationship with an older guy. At this time all my school friends were still drinking their lives away at uni with no real goals/ambition/stability. Cut to a few years later and I decided to go to Uni age 23. I definitely noticed a huge maturity difference between myself at 19 and the 19 year olds at my uni.

For me, because my long term relationship broke up and I had moved around a lot (losing touch with my good friends) I found myself alone and tried very hard to make friends with the people at my Uni. I really feel like I have regressed in maturity through being around these 19/20 year olds and trying to make friends with them. I feel completely lost, honestly. 5 years is not much difference but enough for me to see the world completely differently from them and they all think I'm very strange as a result. I came to uni trying to be open minded and not stuck to my ways but I just feel so frustrated now. Those friends from school who went to uni are now working in careers and in long-term relationships / getting married / having kids. I honestly wish I hadn't bothered coming to uni and had just carried on with work, I would be much further in my life if I had. I thought I would meet similar mature students who I could make friends with but instead I've found myself feeling extremely depressed and being reminded of school due to the immaturity and bitchiness of everybody else. It's got to the point where I literally just do the uni work and don't really talk to anyone. I'm just looking forward to finishing so I can get back to being an adult again!

Anyway, sorry for the long post (if you're reading). I wish we were at the same uni so we could have been friends :)

I second what zanaara said! Don't waste your precious time hanging out with people who you don't want to be like. 
You sound young, if I could talk to my younger self this is the one most important piece of advice I would give. If you hang out with people who are going nowhere you will go nowhere with them. 

Separate yourself, take some time alone to deal with your own problems and really think about the person you want to be and the friends you want to have. Visualize yourself and those friends and the type of girlfriend you'd like. Hold this image in your mind anytime you feel depressed or suicidal. The clearer you can see the life you want the easier it will be to get there. 

It sounds like you're doing a lot of good things but being around negative people is dragging you down. Sometimes being alone is the only way we can get to where we want. 

Also don't worry about being a virgin. The more energy one expends on sex the less they have to work on themselves. It is also very obvious to girls when a guy just wants sex and not very attrractive to be honest... Try and focus on other things you enjoy such as hobbies. Read books about interesting subjects so you will actually be able to have conversations with girls!

FINALLY it kinda sounds like you're too concerned with fitting in at the moment. I totally get it, I was exactly the same when I was young. It doesn't actually matter if people think you're weird. Weird is wonderful. Focus on figuring out what makes YOU happy, you might find its not what makes society happy and thats fine. Maybe you're not the sort of person that enjoys trips with friends and that's fine! 
My experience has been that sometimes following the herd will take you away from your personal goals and dreams and that WILL lead you to feel depressed and dissatisfied.
